### Subtypes across callback boundaries

When a host callback returns a selected `Subtype`, pass the callback and one
valid value of that callback's declared result type through
`with_recovery(function, value)`. The package checks the recovery value before
Lean or the callback runs. Lean then applies the selected constructor to the
callback's actual reply. Constructor rejection raises `LeanBridgeError` with
status 1; an exception raised by the Python function returns as the same
exception object. The recovery value only lets Lean finish the rejected call.
It is never substituted for successful output.

Returned Lean closures accept the generated base Python types and check every
selected `Subtype` leaf before their body runs. This includes the admitted
copied containers, such as options, results and arrays. A rejected call leaves
the closure open, so a later valid call can reuse it. Call `close()` when the
closure is no longer needed. These directional callback checks are implemented
for synchronous copied-value callbacks; retained or asynchronous host callbacks
and owned `Subtype` payloads remain unsupported.

### Subtypes across callback boundaries

When a host callback returns a selected `Subtype`, wrap it with one valid value
of the declared result type: `API.with_recovery(callable, value)`. The generated
package validates that recovery before entering Lean or invoking the callable.
Lean applies the selected constructor to the callable's actual reply. Rejection
raises `API::LeanBridgeError` with status 1, while an exception raised by the
Ruby callable returns as the same exception object. Recovery is used only to
finish the failed Lean call and never becomes successful output.

A returned Lean closure checks selected `Subtype` leaves in its Ruby arguments
before its body runs, including admitted copied containers. Rejection leaves
the closure usable for a later valid call. Call `close` when finished; repeated
close calls are harmless. Directional checks currently require synchronous MRI
callbacks. Retained or asynchronous host callbacks and owned `Subtype` payloads
remain unsupported.

These local runs do not measure dispatch counts or establish hosted
release-floor acceptance.

### Subtypes across callback boundaries

When a host callback returns a selected `Subtype`, pass a valid value of its
declared result type with `with_recovery(callback, value)`. The callback returns
`Result<T, Error>`. The generated crate validates the recovery before entering
Lean or invoking the callback, and Lean applies the selected constructor to the
actual reply. Constructor rejection returns `Error::Native` with code 1. A
callback error or panic is preserved and delivered after the native trampoline
has returned. Recovery only completes the rejected Lean call; it is never
successful output.

Returned Lean closures check selected `Subtype` leaves in borrowed Rust inputs
before their body runs, including admitted copied containers. Rejection leaves
the closure open for later calls. Use `close()` for deterministic release;
repeated calls are harmless. Directional checks are implemented for synchronous
copied-value callbacks. Retained or asynchronous host callbacks and owned
`Subtype` payloads remain unsupported.

edits.current:
Run Python, Ruby and Rust together on a Linux x64 host that meets the generated
package floor, with Python 3.12, MRI Ruby 3.3.12 and the pinned Rust 1.90.0
toolchain:

```sh
source scripts/env.sh
LEAN_BRIDGE_CALLBACK_SUBTYPE_LANGUAGE_PROFILES=python,ruby,rust \
  node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/callback-subtype-language-installed.test.mjs
```

The test builds ordinary-source and independently reviewed wheels, gems and
crates in two combined releases. It verifies each package-set receipt, removes
the author root, installs from copied archives without registry access and runs
independent consumers. Python and Ruby complete fifteen checks per route; Rust
completes seventeen. They cover exact typed recovery, recovery validation before
callback entry, constructor rejection, exception or error preservation, nested
option/result replies, returned-closure input rejection, reuse and idempotent
close. The default record is `build/callback-subtypes/languages.json`.

C/C++ execute closure inputs, Lean-produced results and arguments sent to host callbacks for `Fin` and selected `Subtype` values, including supported copied containers and mixed refined/unrefined arguments. Python, Ruby and Rust execute the same two selected-`Subtype` directions for their admitted copied values. For a host callback result containing a selected `Subtype`, the host supplies one typed recovery value before the call: the C callback descriptor's `recovery` pointer or the generated `with_recovery(callback, value)` API in C++, Python, Ruby and Rust. The public wrapper validates and copies that value before Lean or the callback runs. Lean independently runs the selected checked constructor on every host-produced refined leaf. A rejected recovery prevents the callback from running; a rejected callback result records the first error, suppresses later callbacks and leaves the caller's output unchanged. The recovery exists only so Lean can finish its failure path and is never returned as success. Ordinary and independently reviewed packages exercise the same direction and exact constructor choices. CPAN supplies the same directional contract through `Runtime::Callback`. Nested callbacks, retained or asynchronous callbacks, checked-record callback positions, owned callback Subtypes, .NET, JVM, native PHP and WIT/WASI remain separate work.
